title: React Native and Vega OS integration
lead: These two directories provide source code for integration into external native projects. Passing the repository’s type checks and unit tests does not establish that the resulting apps build or play on a device.

blocks.text: apps/react-native provides App.tsx, the source list, DVR logic, and state management. Its declared dependencies are Expo ~54.0.0, React Native 0.81.5, React 19.1.0, and bitmovin-player-react-native ^1.20.1. It is not a complete Expo app; integrate it into a compatible external project.

blocks.title: External project creation example from the README
blocks.text:
npx create-expo-app@latest dvr-showcase
cd dvr-showcase
npx expo install bitmovin-player-react-native expo-crypto

The dependencies generated by @latest change over time. Compare the generated project with the versions in apps/react-native/package.json. The native Player module requires a development build; Expo Go cannot run it.

items: Run sync-env.sh and build and synchronize the shared UI as described in the common preparation.

Copy App.tsx, src/, and the generated .env from apps/react-native into the external Expo project. The Player license is read from EXPO_PUBLIC_BITMOVIN_PLAYER_LICENSE_KEY, and the optional Analytics license from EXPO_PUBLIC_BITMOVIN_ANALYTICS_LICENSE_KEY.

Render the copied App.tsx component from the external project’s entry point. In an Expo Router project, connect it to the route screen that should display the player; copying the file alone does not replace that screen.
Allow the external app’s bundle identifier or application ID on your Player license and, if used, Analytics license. There is no fixed public application ID for this integration.

For a custom UI, bundle the JavaScript and CSS from assets/webui/ into the external app’s iOS/Android projects, and update WEBUI_JS and WEBUI_CSS in App.tsx to point to the actual files. The current addresses are integration placeholders.
Run an iOS or Android development build from the external Expo project.

blocks.title: Choose the target command in the external Expo project
blocks.text:
npx expo run:ios
npx expo run:android

The screen includes Default, Sports, Live (DVR), and Cinema UI choices; source buttons; Live edge; −10/−30/−60-second controls; Allow DVR; state; and an event log. Changing the UI recreates PlayerPane and reloads the selected source. Source selection is preserved, but playback position and playing state are not guaranteed to continue. A DASH entry in the catalog does not mean it works on every target OS, including iOS.

blocks.title: Check logic and types from the repository root

blocks.text: Type checking covers App.tsx, the source list, and pure logic. It does not verify external Expo project generation, native builds, WebView rendering, or actual playback. Automated native playback tests are not included.

Vega OS is a separate runtime from Android-based Fire TV. apps/vega connects the modular Web Player to a W3C media element and uses React Native/Kepler screen components. It does not use bitmovin-player-ui, which requires a browser document. Dependencies include Player 8.138.0-beta.28, React Native 0.72.0, React 18.2.0, and Amazon device packages.

items: Prepare the Amazon Vega/Kepler development tools and a compatible Fire TV device or Vega simulator. Check each provider’s terms for the CLI, SDK, and device packages.
Integrate the sources into a configured Kepler project. This repository alone does not provide a standalone device build.
Replace src/polyfills.ts with the compatibility layer required by the runtime. Base64, DOMParser, W3C media, and WebCrypto are needed; the minimal template alone cannot provide playback.

Set your licenses in globals in the entry point before registering the app. App.tsx itself does not read .env. The Player’s tweaks.app_id example is com.showcase.dvr.vega; align it with your own configuration and license permissions.
Build, install, and launch from the Kepler project. Check video output, seeking, return to live, recovery after a position expires, and remote controls on the device.

blocks.title: Run from a configured Kepler project
blocks.text:
react-native build-kepler --build-type Debug
kepler device install-app --dir .
kepler device launch-app

The screen includes source selection, Live edge, −10/−30/−60-second controls, Allow DVR, state, and logs. The example enables autoplay and mute. It does not provide dedicated play/pause buttons, audio/subtitle/quality selection, or TV remote key-event handling. DRM modules are also excluded.

blocks.title: Check the core logic from the repository root

blocks.text: Vega type checking covers the core logic and excludes React/Kepler .tsx screens. Session tests use fake media and Player objects. Successful Kepler builds, screen behavior, remote control behavior, and actual playback have not been recorded.
